local_proof.state: Current PROBE target p is being loaded. The one known next operation is PROBE q, q is initially resident, q differs from p, and size(p)+size(q)<=M. The unprotected SPILL plan a evicts q; f1=written(a). The alternative protects q and writes f2. Plans are valid and contain only SPILL actions.
local_proof.unprotected_lower_bound: After a and LOAD(p), q is on disk. Before q can be served it must be loaded, costing size(q)/R whether this occurs in the intervening periodic callback or on miss. With no data-changing operation between these consecutive probes, capacity forces at least d additional SPILL bytes. Additional loads can only increase the required writes.
local_proof.protected_cost: Protect-q plan writes f2 and retains q while LOAD(p) completes. The existing periodic PROBE path performs no IO for an already resident q. Thus, through service of q, it needs neither a q read nor another spill.
local_proof.common_costs: Initial p read and already incurred p miss penalty are common and cancel.
local_proof.local_dominance: (f2-f1)/W <= size(q)/R+d/W implies no greater IO for this fixed p,q service prefix.
local_proof.legacy_boundary: Keep the old size(q)/R+1us acceptance region. A decision newly accepted by the expanded comparison necessarily has credit>1us; its extra write time is then <=size(q)/R+floor(d/2^shift)/W<=size(q)/R+d/W. The inherited +1us region itself has no general IO-dominance proof.
local_proof.cut: After service of the known next q, BEFORE the periodic callback belonging to q.
local_proof.not_claimed: No claim that q must miss: periodic preloading may avoid its miss penalty. No bound on callback D, unknown operations after q, or full Score. Real-arithmetic certificate only; floating comparisons are not machine-certified.
local_proof.legal_information: Uses only current SystemState, one legal next_op and the two already computed plans.
local_proof.integer_domain: For valid plans f1,f2<=U<=M, partition sizes<=M<=4GiB. Deficit arithmetic and f2-f1 are safely int64; max(0,...) precedes the right shift.
